breaking_changes.BC_description: Excess command-arguments now cause an error by default, as 'allowExcessArguments' is set to false by default. Previously, extra arguments were silently accepted. This change affects the 'parse' method of the 'program' object, which is used to parse command-line arguments.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: To adapt, declare expected arguments using 'program.argument()' or suppress the error with 'program.allowExcessArguments()'. Example: Before: program.parse() without argument declaration. After: program.argument('[args...]', 'description') or program.allowExcessArguments(true).

breaking_changes.BC_description: Throw an error during Option constructor call for unsupported option flags, such as multiple characters after a single '-' (e.g., '-abc') or multiple long flags (e.g., '--flag1 --flag2'), which were previously allowed but are now invalid to improve consistency and prevent runtime issues.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Ensure option flags are valid. For short flags, use only one character after a single '-'. For long flags, use a single '--' prefix followed by the flag name. Example before: new Option('-abc', 'description') or new Option('--flag1 --flag2', 'description'). Example after: Use valid flags like new Option('-a', 'description') for short flags or new Option('--abc', 'description') for long flags. If multiple flags are needed, define them separately or use the dual long option support added in Commander 13.1 (e.g., new Option('--es, --ecmascript', 'description')).

breaking_changes.BC_description: Throw an error on multiple calls to '.parse()' if 'storeOptionsAsProperties' is true, which was previously allowed but could cause issues. This change enforces that '.parse()' should only be called once when 'storeOptionsAsProperties' is true to prevent unexpected behavior, while allowing multiple calls when 'storeOptionsAsProperties' is false.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Avoid multiple calls to '.parse()' when 'storeOptionsAsProperties' is true, or set it to false. Example: Before: program.parse(); program.parse(); After: Call '.parse()' only once or use 'storeOptionsAsProperties: false'. For instance, set storeOptionsAsProperties to false in the program configuration: new Commander.Command({ storeOptionsAsProperties: false }); then multiple calls to parse are allowed.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The 'Help.wrap()' method has been removed and refactored into two new methods: 'Help.formatItem()' and 'Help.boxWrap()'. This change was made to improve support for color and styling in help output, treating ANSI escape sequences as zero width during padding and wrapping. The old method is no longer available, and calls to it must be replaced.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace all calls to 'Help.wrap(text)' with either 'Help.formatItem(text)' or 'Help.boxWrap(text)' based on the specific use case. For general text formatting, use 'formatItem()'; for wrapping text in a boxed format, use 'boxWrap()'. Example: Before: helpInstance.wrap('some text'); After: helpInstance.formatItem('some text') or helpInstance.boxWrap('some text').
